items.q: Match the following G stage with its GFR (ml/min) — 1) G1  2) G3a  3) G4  4) G5 … A) <15  B) ≥90  C) 15-29  D) 45-59
The GFR range for stage G2 is:
The GFR range for stage G3b is:
Fill up: In the G table, stage G1 (GFR ≥90) qualifies only when ______ / biochemical / histological evidence is positive.
items.exp: G1: ≥90 ml/min → radiological / biochemical / histological evidence (+). (Book p806)

items.q: In the G table, stage G5 (GFR <15) is labelled as:
items.exp: G5: <15 ml/min → ESRD (uremic phase); mx: dialysis. (Book p806)

items.q: Match the following A stage with its urine albumin-creatinine ratio — 1) A1  2) A2  3) A3 … A) >300 mg/g — severely ↑↑  B) ≤30 mg/g — normal  C) 30-300 mg/g — moderately ↑
items.exp: A - ACR: A1 ≤30 mg/g normal; A2 30-300 mg/g moderately ↑; A3 >300 mg/g severely ↑↑. (Book p806)

items.q: The upper limit of the A2 albuminuria band is:
A3 corresponds to an ACR above 300 mg/g and is described as severely raised.
opts: True, but only with GFR below 15

items.q: A CKD patient has a GFR of 22 ml/min and an ACR of 450 mg/g. The staging is:
The A category of the classification is built on which ratio (ACR)?
items.exp: A - ACR (urine albumin creatine ratio) as printed on the page. (Book p806)
